title: Tensor detection through a finite field-product embedding
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] [def-pc-field-extension], let $A,B$ be commutative $k$-algebras, let $I$ be a finite set, and let $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ be extension fields of $k$. Put $P=\prod_{i\in I}K_i$ with coordinatewise operations, and let $j:B\to P$ be an injective unital $k$-algebra homomorphism. Use tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with multiplication $(x\otimes a)(y\otimes b)=xy\otimes ab$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Then the canonical map $\Phi:P\otimes_kA\to\prod_{i\in I}(K_i\otimes_kA)$, $(x_i)_i\otimes a\mapsto(x_i\otimes a)_i$, is a unital $k$-algebra isomorphism, and the map $\Theta:B\otimes_kA\to\prod_{i\in I}(K_i\otimes_kA)$, $b\otimes a\mapsto(j(b)_i\otimes a)_i$, is injective. If $A\otimes_kK_i$ is reduced for every $i\in I$, then $B\otimes_kA$ is reduced. Reduced means that the only nilpotent element is zero. The set $I$ may be empty, with empty product the zero ring; neither $A$ nor $B$ is assumed nonzero or finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 034N (lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change), proof, last two sentences: passage through a finite product of fields and reducedness after tensoring.

proof.text: For each $i$, let $p_i:P\to K_i$ be projection and let $s_i:K_i\to P$ insert an element in coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere; these are $k$-linear, and $s_i$ need not preserve the ring unit. Enumerate the finite set $I$ as $i_1,\dots,i_t$ with $t=|I|\ge0$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] with $R=k$, $P_m=K_{i_m}$ for $1\le m\le t$, and $N=A$: there is a unique $k$-linear map $\Phi:P\otimes_kA\to\prod_{i\in I}(K_i\otimes_kA)$ with $(x_i)_i\otimes a\mapsto(x_i\otimes a)_i$, i.e. with $i$-coordinate $p_i\otimes1_A$, and it is an isomorphism of $k$-modules. Explicitly, its inverse is $\Psi((z_i)_i)=\sum_{i\in I}(s_i\otimes1_A)(z_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]: on pure tensors $p_js_i=\delta_{ij}$ gives $\Phi\Psi=1$ and $\sum_is_ip_i=1_P$ gives $\Psi\Phi=1$. For $I=\varnothing$ the leaf's case $t=0$ applies: $P=0$ and $P\otimes_kA=0$.

source.place: Tag 034N (lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change), proof, last two sentences, expanded finite-product tensor argument; tensor universal property in Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: The linear isomorphism $\Phi$ preserves multiplication: for pure tensors $x\otimes a,y\otimes b$, its $i$-coordinate on their product is $x_iy_i\otimes ab=(x_i\otimes a)(y_i\otimes b)$. Bilinearity of multiplication and generation by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extend the equality to all elements. Its value on $1_P\otimes1_A$ is $(1_{K_i}\otimes1_A)_i$, the target unit. Thus it is a unital $k$-algebra isomorphism, including the empty-product case. Likewise the tensor-induced map $j\otimes1_A$ is multiplicative and unital: on pure tensors the calculation is $j(bb')\otimes aa'=j(b)j(b')\otimes aa'$, and the unit maps to $j(1_B)\otimes1_A=1_P\otimes1_A$.

source.place: Tag 034N (lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change), proof, last two sentences, expanded finite-product tensor argument; tensor universal property in Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: The $k$-module $A$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the exact sequence $0\to B\xrightarrow{j}P\to P/j(B)$ of $k$-modules; the quotient here is a module quotient, not a quotient algebra. It follows that $j\otimes1_A:B\otimes_kA\to P\otimes_kA$ is injective. Its composite with the isomorphism $\Phi$ is injective and on $b\otimes a$ has coordinates $j(b)_i\otimes a$. This composite is exactly $\Theta$. No finiteness condition on the vector spaces is used.

source.place: Tag 034N (lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change), proof, last two sentences, expanded finite-product tensor argument; tensor universal property in Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: Assume each $A\otimes_kK_i$ is reduced. The swap $\tau_i:K_i\otimes_kA\to A\otimes_kK_i$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm] sends $t\otimes a$ to $a\otimes t$. It is a ring isomorphism: the product formula gives $\tau_i((t\otimes a)(u\otimes b))=ab\otimes tu=(a\otimes t)(b\otimes u)$, extended by bilinearity, and it preserves $1\otimes1$. By step 2, $\Theta=\Phi\circ(j\otimes1_A)$ (step 3) is multiplicative. If $z\in B\otimes_kA$ satisfies $z^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$, then $\Theta(z)^n=\Theta(z^n)=0$, so $\tau_i(\Theta(z)_i)^n=0$ for every $i$. Reducedness of $A\otimes_kK_i$ implies $\tau_i(\Theta(z)_i)=0$, so each $\Theta(z)_i=0$. Thus $\Theta(z)=0$ and its injectivity gives $z=0$. For $I=\varnothing$, the coordinate conclusion is vacuous and equality in the singleton empty product still gives $\Theta(z)=0$; for zero $A$ or $B$ the same calculation applies.
